name: Joe Lombardi

views.text: A quarterback earns trust by running the offense cleanly and not turning a bad call into a disaster.
New plays always look shaky for a few days; repetition is what turns a rookie into someone who looks like a veteran.
When protection breaks down the whole offense owns it, not only the quarterback or the play-caller.
Coordinators get fired when offenses stall; that is the job, and you learn from each stop.
In a head coach's system, the coordinator's work is the install, the details and the quarterback's comfort.
A smart, prepared rookie is everything you hope for, but footwork errors still have to be coached hard.

signatures: praises a quarterback's preparation first, then names one technical fix
keeps answers about the offense's direction short and points to the head coach's plan
want: to be the trusted quarterback mind behind a winning offense, with his long partnership with Payton paying off a second time
fear: that repeated coordinator firings leave him seen as a lieutenant who never quite runs the show
voice: Calm, plain and technical, closer to a quarterbacks-room teacher than a showman. He speaks well of players, especially quarterbacks, in measured terms, explains what a rep looked like rather than making predictions, and defers on big-picture questions to the head coach.

evidence.summary: Staff announcement: Joe Lombardi named offensive coordinator after 2021-22 as Chargers OC, two Detroit seasons as OC, and 12 seasons with Payton's Saints as an assistant and quarterbacks coach; Vance Joseph returns as defensive coordinator after four years running Arizona's defense, having been Denver's head coach in 2017-18. Lists titles only; does not say who calls plays.

Detroit fires Lombardi midway through his second season as OC after a 1-6 start and a seven-sack loss to Minnesota; quarterbacks coach Jim Bob Cooter takes over. A staffing report; says nothing about his personality.

Matthew Stafford calls Lombardi a very talented coordinator and says players share responsibility for the offense's failures. One player's public support after the firing; date taken from the news cycle around the firing.
The Chargers keep Staley but fire Lombardi and the quarterbacks coach after blowing a 27-0 playoff lead at Jacksonville; Lombardi had been OC since 2021. Staffing report.

Lombardi credits Nix's camp progress to growing comfort with huddle calls and checks, praises his intelligence and preparation, notes new plays take a few days of reps, and says he judges quarterbacks on clean operation and sound choices. Upbeat but measured tone.

review.notes: Thin coverage: Lombardi does not call plays in Denver, so most sources are staffing reports; sliders left neutral.
